planner.question: Can unrestricted stage failures be transferred to unique-witness selectors with quantified seed mass, without assuming an efficient deterministic isolation oracle?

construct.claim: Under NP!=RP, for each fixed k the uniquely satisfiable B_k(n+(n+1)^2) has at least 2^((n+1)^2-3) members at unbounded n.
construct.scope: Same U, explicit normalized selector encoding and exact stage clocks on every constructed selector; arbitrary original formulas; conditional isolation transfer.
construct.derivation: Pairwise-independent affine hash yields >=3/16 isolation probability at some r; if all inputs have inverse-polynomial success probability for some r, exact stage trials give RP. Injective encoding converts conditional bad mass to counts.
unresolved_steps: Unconditional cubic-stage infinitude and all-exponent failure.
candidate_tests: Exact small seed census, normalized CNF extension and actual stage projection.

alternative.claim: Eventual absence of unique residuals at some k implies NP=RP; with an efficient deterministic isolating-list constructor it implies P=NP.
alternative.scope: Same U, explicit normalized selector encoding and exact stage clocks on every constructed selector; arbitrary original formulas; conditional isolation transfer.
alternative.derivation: Try all row counts and random seeds, or an explicitly supplied polynomial isolating list; union bound yields nonuniform common list only.
unresolved_steps: Uniform deterministic isolation-list discovery and absence of unique residuals.
candidate_tests: Pairwise independence, exact rational union bound, fallback controls.
